classification.difficultyReason: Complete a right triangle using the symmetric roof's unsupplied altitude and half-width, then use inverse tangent and relate the half-apex angle to the full angle between the beams.

content.prompt: A roof truss is 6.8 m wide and 1.5 m high. Calculate the angle $\theta$ between the two beams, correct to the nearest degree.

spec.description: Symmetric open roof profile with a centred apex, full interior apex angle and separate width and height dimension arrows. No base or altitude is supplied. Decorative blue outlines are rendered in house black.
spec.mathematics: Width 6.8 m; perpendicular height 1.5 m; theta is the full included angle between equal sloping beams.
spec.answerVisibility: Givens only; no calculated angle or construction line.

answer.short:
$132^\circ$.

Split the symmetric truss into two right triangles and double the half-apex angle.
answer.worked:
Draw the perpendicular from the apex to the midpoint of the width. Each half has horizontal length $6.8\div2=3.4$ m and vertical height 1.5 m. Let the half-apex angle be $\alpha$.

$$\begin{align*}\tan\alpha&=\frac{3.4}{1.5}\\\alpha&=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{3.4}{1.5}\right)\\\theta&=2\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{3.4}{1.5}\right)\\\theta&\approx132^\circ\end{align*}$$
